correctness.rationale: P1--P4 plus identity and semicomplementation yield the finite row normal form; P5 is precisely cross-antecedent coherence. On three atoms, each doubleton has at most 18 explicit candidates and the 64 singleton negation rows split into 16 directed-graph orbits, giving the exact weighted sum 7820. In the F case polarity self-adjointness restricts negation to 8 simple undirected graphs, with graph-indexed fiber counts 729, 81, 16, 1, giving 1021. A separate direct evaluation of all original P1--P5 and T/F axioms over each of the generated operations passed. The 1- and 2-atom cases establish the strict minimum.

originality.rationale: Holliday establishes P1--P5 and representation results, and Chen formulates the T/F classes and proves completeness/finite model property, but their inspected results do not give an exact census of all binary operations on the eight-element Boolean carrier. Related public published-finding corpus results enumerate preconditionals on chains, which are not Boolean three-atom carriers. Previously available unary negation counts 125 and 8 do not determine 7820 and 1021 binary lifts. Directed-graph and exact-number searches identified no covering record. Historical priority remains a risk; unsuccessful searches do not establish uniqueness.
residual_risks: Search and finite full-text inspection cannot establish absolute novelty; an unlocated classical or contemporary enumeration could dominate this small-carrier result.
The two exact numbers are given for a labelled Boolean algebra and should not be confused with the number of isomorphism classes.
The related public finite-chain results were compared at the title/summary level rather than by full-text retrieval, but their objects are plainly nonisomorphic to the eight-element Boolean carrier.

value.rationale: The actual binary operator is the logical connective of interest; its unary negation can conceal substantial extra expressive structure. This finite natural boundary is the first Boolean algebra on which unary negation fails to determine T/F implication, and one F-negation has 729 distinct binary lifts. Complete counts and fiber classification for the smallest meaningful case are motivated by conditional-logical definability and cannot be inferred from unary reduct counts alone. No general downstream theorem is claimed or needed.
